messages:
Sam C. (Acme Corp): Hey folks — we just finished a group sync from Okta and noticed ~20 users in the 'DataScience' group lost access to the app. Some were fully deprovisioned (no longer listed in the org). Any idea what might cause bulk removals?

Maya K. (CS): hey Sam, sorry about this. Are they missing the role mapping (ds-editor) or were their accounts deleted entirely? Can you paste the SCIM request payload or connector logs? :eyes: 

Sam C. (Acme Corp): Most are showing as removed from the org entirely. We pushed a group push this morning. Snapshot of the SCIM PATCH we sent (redacted):

```json
{
  "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"],
  "Operations": [
    {
      "op": "replace",
      "path": "members",
      "value": [
        { "value": "alice@acme.com", "display": "Alice" },
        { "value": "bob@acme.com", "display": "Bob" },
        ...
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Sam C. (Acme Corp): Note: Okta was set to send email addresses in `members.value` (we assumed matching by email).

Maya K. (CS): got it. Two quick checks: 1) Do you have an externalId -> role mapping configured, or are you using email-based matching in our SCIM connector? 2) Any error traces from our side? I can open an account-level trace.

Sam C. (Acme Corp): We're using the default mapping from onboarding — we set group->role by group name (DataScience -> ds-editor). We didn't configure externalId mappings explicitly. On Okta we left "members.value" as email.

Okta Integration Bot: Sync run id 2023-11-20T13:02:34Z: Group push started for group 'DataScience'. 245 members processed. 235 matched; 10 not matched. 10 members removed from org due to unmatched mapping.

Jo Gomez (SRE): that bot log is useful. the phrasing "removed from org due to unmatched mapping" — sounds like our SCIM matcher attempted to resolve `members.value` to existing users by id and fell back to a strict rule that treated unmatched entries as removals instead of email matches. can you upload the connector trace?

Sam C. (Acme Corp): attaching a trimmed connector trace (copied):

```
[2023-11-20T13:02:35Z] PATCH /scim/v2/Groups/9a8b... - body members[0].value="alice@acme.com"
[2023-11-20T13:02:35Z] lookupUserById("alice@acme.com") -> not found
[2023-11-20T13:02:35Z] lookupUserByEmail("alice@acme.com") -> found user id u-12345
[2023-11-20T13:02:35Z] groupMemberAdd(Group=9a8b..., User=u-12345) -> OK
[2023-11-20T13:02:35Z] lookupUserById("bob@acme.com") -> not found
[2023-11-20T13:02:35Z] lookupUserByEmail("bob@acme.com") -> NOT FOUND
[2023-11-20T13:02:35Z] memberNotMatched -> scheduleUserRemoval(User: u-99999)
```

Sam C. (Acme Corp): u-99999 was an old placeholder user that had been merged months ago. That's why it got removed.

Ashok P. (Eng): ok this is helpful. root cause summary (prelim): our SCIM group reconciliation currently treats a members list as authoritative and performs a 2-step reconciliation: 1) map incoming member values to canonical user ids; 2) any canonical members not present in the incoming set are removed. the problem: when `members.value` is an email, we try `lookupById` first (expecting a Redwood user id), then fallback to email. But if the fallback fails (email not found) we still consider that slot "intended to be a different user" and may remove a previously-matched placeholder user. we should not remove existing users if we can't confirm the incoming value refers to a different user.

Maya K. (CS): Ashok, is there any immediate mitigatiom we can run for the customer? Sam, we need to restore the deleted users asap.

Ashok P. (Eng): mitigation steps: 1) stop the scheduled group sync in Okta (so no more patches) 2) run a restore job to re-create the removed members from audit trail (we have their user ids in the audit log) — I can trigger a one-off restore if you give approval. 3) short-term config change: switch the connector to use email matching explicitly instead of sending email in `members.value` if possible, or configure our SCIM matcher to prefer email when the value is an email pattern.

Sam C. (Acme Corp): please trigger restore. we'll pause the Okta group push immediately. thanks. :pray:

Jo Gomez (SRE): I'm triggering the restore job now. job id rstr-20231120-37. ETA ~3m. I'll DM details when done.

Okta Integration Bot: Restore job rstr-20231120-37: restoring 10 users -> completed successfully.

Sam C. (Acme Corp): I can confirm 9/10 users are back in the org; one still missing (charlie@acme.com).

Ashok P. (Eng): checking logs for charlie.

[small pause]

Ashok P. (Eng): found why charlie didn't restore: the audit record showed the original user id was already recycled (u-99999 reused) and our restore job skipped due to id collision. I will escalate to eng-runtime to add a safety: when a restore finds an id collision, we should create a new user and re-assign historical attributes instead of skipping.

Maya K. (CS): action items for Acme: 1) Pause Okta pushes until we confirm mapping change. 2) Confirm whether Okta can send `members.value` as user externalId (our recommended flow) or continue sending email but set connector to "match on email". 3) Provide a copy of your group push settings.

Sam C. (Acme Corp): we can change Okta to send externalId (will take ~30m), but curious what the long-term fix is on your side.

Ashok P. (Eng): long-term fix (eng): change reconciliation logic to treat unmatched incoming member entries as "possible new member" rather than a deterministic removal trigger. specific proposal:

```
- if members.value matches uuid pattern -> lookup by id only
- else if members.value matches email pattern -> lookup by email first, fall back to id
- if lookup fails -> do not remove existing canonical members; instead mark group as "pending verification" and open an admin notification with the list of unmatched entries
```

Ashok P. (Eng): I'll put up a PR with the change and a migration that replays 7 days of group syncs to ensure no regressions.

Maya K. (CS): thanks. Sam, after you switch Okta to externalId or enable email matching, can you re-test with a small test group (5 users) and ping us? we'll keep monitoring.

Sam C. (Acme Corp): will do. one more Q — is there any token scope/auth issue here? our security team asked if we were missing scim write perms because we saw some 403s earlier in a different run.

Jo Gomez (SRE): I scanned the earlier traces: there were a handful of 403s from Okta to our SCIM endpoint due to a rotated token in their integration (scim.write). Okta retried and then succeeded once token was updated. that's unrelated to this reconciliation logic but worth noting: brief auth failures + the strict reconciliation combined to cause the removals.

Maya K. (CS): summary for thread (so we have everything):
- root cause: reconciliation logic removed canonical users when incoming `members.value` couldn't be resolved; Okta was sending emails in `members.value` and some emails didn't match existing accounts (old placeholders) => removals
- immediate mitigation: Okta paused, restore job run, 9/10 recovered; charlie had id collision and will be manually recreated by eng runtime
- short-term customer action: change Okta to send externalId or enable "match on email"; test on small group
- long-term eng fix: update matcher to prefer email when pattern matches; treat unmatched entries as pending verification rather than automatic removals

Ashok P. (Eng): I'll open ENG ticket RN and link it here once PR is posted.

Maya K. (CS): assigning follow-ups: @Ashok P. will own the runtime PR (ENG-3456), @Jo will confirm restore completion and charlie recreation, @Sam will pause Okta and update mapping. I'll follow up with Acme in 24h to confirm. :thumbsup:

Sam C. (Acme Corp): thanks everyone. appreciate the quick turnaround.
